title: Level 3 (Advanced) - C-8
notes:
West leads the ♣Q against 6♥. West's lead is won by South. South is fortunate that he did not receive a spade lead, but he still must play carefully. Dummy's diamonds will provide enough discards for South's spade and club losers. There is a certain loser in the trump suit, however, and that suit must be 3-2 for the contract to have a chance.

South should try to arrange to run dummy's diamonds after drawing all of the outstanding trumps. South should begin by cashing the ♦A. A top trump is won in dummy, but the second round of trumps should be ducked. South can win the spade or club return. Dummy is entered in hearts, drawing the last of the defensive trumps. The diamond suit can now be run in comfort.

Notice that it is inferior to duck the first round of trump after cashing the ♦A. If one of the defenders started with a doubleton heart and a singleton club, the defense would be able to take a club ruff. Winning a round of trump before ducking a round effectively guards against this possibility.
